name: How long does a pool remodel take in Los Angeles from demolition to fill-up?

mainEntity.name: How long does a pool remodel take in Los Angeles from demolition to fill-up?
mainEntity.text: How long does a pool remodel take in Los Angeles from demolition to fill-up?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool remodel timeline in Los Angeles depends on whether the work is cosmetic or structural. A simple resurfacing may finish in a couple of weeks, while a full remodel with tile, coping, equipment changes, deck repairs, or spa additions can stretch much longer. The biggest schedule variables are permit needs, inspection timing, material availability, and unexpected repairs discovered after demolition. Homeowners should ask for a phase-by-phase schedule that includes drain-out, demolition, shell repair, plumbing or electrical rough-in, tile and coping installation, plaster or pebble application, curing time, and final fill. Weather can also delay finish work, especially when temperatures or humidity affect curing. If the remodel includes automation, heaters, lights, or gas work, coordination with specialty trades can add days or weeks. A realistic contractor schedule should also explain when the pool can be used again, not just when construction is “done.” The finish may need curing time before chemical balancing and swimming are safe.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most Los Angeles pool remodels take a few weeks, but the timeline depends on scope, permits, material lead times, inspection scheduling, and weather. A surface-only remodel is faster than a project that includes plumbing, electrical, deck work, or structural changes. The fill-up usually happens only after finishes cure and final checks are complete.
